attempts.hypothesis: I am using the orbital hints as a value-weighted tour, with reactive obstacle avoidance, on-line energy/fault adaptation, local search for hint error, and conservative sample returns.

The previous run oscillated violently due to aggressive steering and asymmetric motors with dead zones; I'm rewriting the controller with heavily EMA-smoothed, rate-limited proportional steering, GPS heading bias correction, adaptive motor trim, tighter obstacle avoidance, and robust sampling/drilli

Motor asymmetry (right motor ~1.3x stronger) caused all previous attempts to curve in circles and crash; this version measures motor gains online from wheel speed feedback and compensates commands to achieve desired wheel speeds, uses dead-reckoning heading with GPS correction, and eliminates spinni
I believe this is a partially observed, fault-prone navigation and energy-planning problem, so I’m using adaptive sensing, conservative obstacle avoidance, and deliberate sample returns.
The first run mostly spun in place, so I’m replacing the aggressive steering with a damped wheel-speed controller and persistent, energy-aware sampling and return logic.
Nearby site readings and the base beacon are actionable, so I’m replacing the brittle search with progressing waypoints, stopped drilling, and conservative return budgeting.

The trace shows the rover stopping after only a few metres, so I’m replacing the brittle planning with persistent search waypoints and a simpler feedback controller that keeps exploring, sampling and returning.

I believe the previous controllers could settle into a no-progress state, so this version keeps a persistent coverage target, drives it with direct feedback, samples detected sites opportunistically, and returns with an energy reserve.
I believe the earlier runs were trapped by overconservative energy gating and unstable steering, so I’m using bounded adaptive drive control, local site interception, and return-safe waypoints.

I believe the zero-score traces are dominated by compass/GPS faults and no-progress loops near sites, so I’m simplifying pose fusion, adding escape recovery, and protecting a full drill dwell before returning.

I believe the previous run found a site but lost most of the mission in a navigation loop, so I’m keeping persistent hint search and direct sampling while adding faster stuck recovery and more cautious driving and return planning.

attempts.hypothesis: I’ll treat this as an unknown differential-drive world and use online calibration, occupancy-grid path planning with reactive safety, hint-driven site search, conservative energy/time return logic, and adaptive speed control.

I’m using a conservative, self-calibrating differential-drive controller with online heading/motor correction, reactive ray safety, coarse occupancy-grid path planning, hint search, opportunistic sampling, and battery/time-based returns.

I’m replacing the fragile map-planner with a simpler adaptive rover that calibrates compass bias by GPS motion, uses direct relative bearings for sites/beacon, samples opportunistically, searches around hints, and returns conservatively with explicit battery/time margins.

I’m simplifying the controller around stable closed-loop wheel-speed holding, robust GPS/compass fusion, fast opportunistic sampling, and time-boxed hint searches so a false positive cannot consume the mission.

I’m keeping the controller deliberately simpler and more robust: direct relative-bearing site capture, hard-stabilized drilling, timeboxed hint searches, and conservative return/battery logic, because prior runs appeared to stop on a site but fail the still-drill condition.

Prior runs reached a site but active position holding spun the wheels and broke the six-second drill, so I’m replacing acquisition/holding with direct relative-bearing capture, a strict low-wheel-speed start condition, a gentle zero-speed lock during drilling, and guaranteed return after the first s

The critical failure was waiting for a GPS-derived "still" condition before drilling, so I am switching to immediate site-local braking with drill held while speed is managed only by wheel feedback, plus a simpler timeout-driven hint search and conservative return-after-sample strategy.

I’m keeping the proven direct-site sampling behavior but making the rover much safer: a sub-1 m/s speed ceiling, stronger obstacle braking, local occupancy-grid planning with A*, persistent wall/avoidance side, and conservative energy/time returns so faults and missed rays cannot cause another high-

I assume hints are roughly right and search with a spiral when a hint has no site, use site and beacon bearings for final approach, and fuse compass with wheel-speed gyro and GPS-learned compass offset; this first attempt is a robust baseline to tune from the logs.

Attempt 1 never drilled and died against a rock at speed, so I'm assuming the hints are roughly right, the site-within-8 m signal is accurate, and speed must be capped by ray clearance; this version uses ray-scaled speed, pivot escape, a spiral search around each hint, and a grid explore fallback.

Attempt 2 never completed a drill (the 30 s drill timeout fired) and deadlocked behind a rock with near-zero commands, so this version uses a gentler still-hold with a pitch feedforward, obstacle-aware steering that resolves head-on blocks, and position-based stuck detection with escapes that give u

Attempt 3 never delivered because it explored instead of docking and its steering gain made the rover spin and overshoot, so this version docks after collecting a few samples, uses a gentler gap-following steer with proportional turn and deadzone, and searches each hint with a tighter spiral.

Attempt 4 delivered only 3 value and then spent about 900 s in a bump-escape loop near (238, 200), so this version caps forward speed by ray clearance, avoids the dead zone near 0.2, uses wheel-speed stall detection with a bounded escape sequence that gives up on a target after repeated escapes, and

Attempt 5 delivered only 14 value because it crawled at about 0.8 m/s and lost time to rock escapes and a frozen GPS, so I'm raising cruise speed where the rays show clear space, keeping the ray-based braking, and making the time-feasibility checks less conservative.

Attempt 6 delivered only 3 samples because it wandered around rocks and spent about 330 s returning to base, so I'm adding a remembered occupancy grid from the rays with A* routing for long trips (hint, base, explore) while keeping the attempt-6 local driver and the hold, drill and escape logic.

Attempt 7's crash came from carrying 1.1–1.9 m/s into rock faces the rays only saw late, so I'm reverting to the crash-free attempt-6 driver and adding a stricter speed cap, a turning-speed limit and a front-ray brake.
